questions.explain: A recurrence of the same condition within six months is treated as a continuation of the first claim: benefits resume with no new elimination period, but the benefit period is reduced by what was already paid (5 - 2 = 3 years). After six months, it would be a new claim.

questions.q: Leo's disability policy includes waiver of premium and premium refund. He becomes disabled and pays two premiums while his claim is being set up. Once benefits begin, what happens?
options: Premiums are waived only after he has been disabled for a full year
Premiums continue, but are deducted from each benefit payment he receives
Premiums are waived while he receives benefits, but the two he paid are kept
Premiums are waived while he receives benefits, and the two he paid are refunded
questions.explain: Under this optional feature, the insurer waives premiums while the insured is receiving benefits and returns premiums paid during the illness period. Some contracts also extend the waiver to partial disability.

questions.q: Daniel's disability policy has a future coverage option he can exercise every two years until age 50. His income has risen, but his health has declined. What can he do at the next option date?
options: Buy unlimited extra coverage, since the option overrides the income limits
Buy more coverage only if he passes a medical, since his health has changed
Buy more coverage regardless of his health, within the insurer's income limits
Nothing, since the option can be used only if his health is unchanged
questions.explain: A future coverage option lets the insured buy additional coverage at set intervals regardless of health status, up to the insurer's maximum percentage of income and dollar cap. Once the cap is reached, coverage can't be increased.

questions.q: A Quebec insurer issues a health insurance policy to Chloé, who has met every requirement except paying the initial premium. Which is correct?
options: It can be in force; cancelling for non-payment requires 15 days' written notice
It is not in force until the initial premium is paid, exactly as with life insurance
It can be in force, but the insurer may cancel it at any time without any notice
It is in force only during a 30-day grace period, after which it lapses automatically
questions.explain: For health policies issued in Quebec, paying the initial premium is not a requirement for the contract to begin, unlike life insurance. If the insurer wants to cancel for non-payment of the initial premium, it must give the insured 15 days' written notice.

questions.q: A negligent driver damages Selena's car. Her insurer pays the $1,000 repair bill and then pursues the other driver to recover it. This is an example of:
options: Co-insurance
Subrogation
Excess insurance
Apportionment
questions.explain: Subrogation substitutes the insurer for the insured to claim indemnity from a responsible third party, giving the insurer the ability to collect damages from a negligent driver after paying its own insured.

questions.q: After her insurer pays for her damaged car, Jo signs an agreement releasing the at-fault driver from all further claims, hoping to avoid a dispute. Which subrogation principle has she breached?
options: Recoveries go first to the insurer and only then to the insured
The insurer cannot subrogate against its own insured to reduce its obligation
Subrogation does not apply to life and most health insurance contracts
The insured cannot stand in the way of the insurer's subrogation rights
questions.explain: Once the insurer has paid, it is entitled to pursue the negligent party, and the insured cannot block those rights. Insurers may choose to waive subrogation, but the insured cannot waive it for them. (If the policy is silent, recoveries go to the insured first, until fully indemnified.)

questions.q: Subrogation does not apply to life insurance or to most health insurance contracts.
options: True
False
questions.explain: True. This is one of the five general principles of subrogation. Subrogation is a feature of general (property and casualty) insurance, letting the insurer recover from a negligent third party.
